criteria.requirement: Aliases resolve deterministically.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Glossary integrity rejects duplicate forms, conflicting aliases, missing abbreviation forms and alias/term mismatches, and preserves punctuation while ignoring case; validate passes on the corpus.

criteria.requirement: Other corpus objects can reference glossary IDs.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Rules cite terms through term_refs and timing_refs; pilot integrity links them to glossary ids and rejects a non-temporal timing reference (phase-four schema test).

criteria.requirement: All pilot material validates.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: The pilot records validate with the whole corpus (npm run validate) and the pilot schema tests pass.

criteria.requirement: No pilot rule requires arbitrary prose-only escape hatches for its main mechanic.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: The pilot ledger maps each pilot mechanic to typed rules/procedures; uncertainties are issues, not prose escape hatches; rule fixtures execute them.

criteria.requirement: Provenance is sufficient to locate the source.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Every record carries document/file/pdf_page/printed_page/heading, checked against pages.yaml (including file identity on glossary provenance).

criteria.requirement: Exceptions can be represented directly.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Exceptions are modelled as overriding rules (for example the thief higher-tier exception suppresses the two-card choice) and tested.

criteria.requirement: Tables round-trip without losing information.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Table rows keep printed and typed cells; the validator rejects missing/extra columns, printed/typed mismatches and partial selections that disagree with source rows.

criteria.requirement: Pilot examples can become executable tests.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: YAML fixtures under tests/examples run through the test interpreter, including the transcribed book example.

criteria.requirement: Common rule primitives are reusable references.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: All 21 priority areas have reusable core.* / character.* rules that later records reference; dangling row rule references are rejected.

criteria.requirement: Later rules do not need to redefine basic check logic.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Check logic lives once in core.check.* and is referenced by later procedures and rules.

criteria.requirement: Timing terms have canonical IDs.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Timing terms are temporal_scope glossary ids; timing_refs must target them.

criteria.requirement: Resource/stat modifications are typed.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Rule effects are typed set/add/require/lookup operations on declared, typed fields with bounds; modifier channels are distinct fields.

criteria.requirement: Every extracted table preserves all rows and columns.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: All 213 canonical tables are completeness: complete; the validator rejects any row whose cells do not match the column set; per-table cell-matrix tests cover the catalogue tables.

criteria.requirement: Every row has stable meaning.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Row ids are unique per table and keep source_row provenance; entity links to rows are reciprocal and structural rows cannot carry entities.

criteria.requirement: Dice expressions are typed.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Dice cells are typed and checked against their printed notation, but 135 table rows print dice inside text cells and 63 of them have no linked rule that types the expression (for example table.magic.miscast rows 4/7/8/10, table.quest.stop_heretics.demons, table.settlement.quest_sites, the table.treasure.furniture.* rows).
remaining_work: Type the dice expressions held only in text cells of those 63 rows (dice cell, composite cell or linked rule), keeping the printed text.

criteria.requirement: Entity references resolve.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Entity, table-row, rule and section references are link-checked by pilot integrity; validate passes.

criteria.requirement: Embedded restrictions are converted into rules where appropriate.

remaining_work: Audit catalogue text cells and entity descriptions for embedded restrictions not yet converted to rules; Step 2 reconciliation and Phase 9 review of each catalogue chapter (docs/corpus-completion-plan.md) cover this.

criteria.requirement: Major game loops are explicitly modeled.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Dungeon turn, dungeon generation/route, battle (state_machine.battle), combat, travel, settlement visit, quest acceptance/departure/dungeon lifecycle (state_machine.quest_dungeon), character creation and levelling are modelled; Package F is accepted.

criteria.requirement: Procedure steps reference atomic rules rather than duplicate them.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Procedure steps cite rules through rule_refs and the validator resolves them, but nothing checks that step effects do not restate rule content; several quest procedures set printed values directly.
remaining_work: Audit procedure step effects for duplicated rule content; this is the Phase 7 duplicate/summary detection in docs/corpus-completion-plan.md Step 4.

criteria.requirement: State-machine transitions have documented triggers.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: The schema requires event, target and source_text on every transition; both state machines validate and the battle machine test checks documented triggers.

criteria.requirement: Branches and terminal states are source-backed.
criteria.finding: 7 October 2026: Every procedure step (including conditional branches) requires source_text; terminal states cannot have outgoing transitions and every transition into one carries source_text.
